_comment: S3 bucket policy — agrisync-raw-ap-south-1. TLS-only. Safe to apply now.
spec: FINAL_SERVER_AUTHORITATIVE_EXECUTION_PLAN §11 (S11-infra-author)
LIVE STATE CAPTURED 2026-08-15 (read-only, aws s3api get-bucket-policy):
NoSuchBucketPolicy — this bucket has NO policy today. Rollback:
aws s3api delete-bucket-policy --bucket agrisync-raw-ap-south-1 --region ap-south-1
=== ROUND 1 REVIEW FINDING C1 — FIX APPLIED 2026-08-15 ===
This file used to also carry a DenyMissingEncryptionHeader statement,
labelled 'Phase 1, safe to apply now'. It was NOT safe: the
s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption condition key reflects the REQUEST HEADER a
writer sends, not the bucket's default encryption — a Null-condition Deny on
s3:PutObject denies every write that omits the header regardless of what
default encryption would otherwise have applied, and the same Deny covers
multipart UploadPart, which structurally cannot carry that header at all.
This is the identical statement/identical reasoning error as
aws/uploads/bucket-policy.json used to carry — see that file's C1 note for
the two concrete hazards. THE SHARP EDGE HERE, specifically: this bucket's
write path (S3RawBlobStore.PutAsync) SWALLOWS the exception on a failed
PutObject. If this Deny had been applied and anything about the write path
changed to stop sending the header (a bug, a future refactor, an admin
script bypassing S3RawBlobStore), the failure would be invisible — farmers
would get HTTP 200 while their evidence silently stopped being retained.
That is the exact failure class §11 exists to end, reintroduced by a
statement labelled safe.
The encryption-header-deny statement is moved to:
aws/raw/bucket-policy-encryption-deny.NOT-VERIFIED-DO-NOT-APPLY.json
— a SEPARATE hazard from, and a separate file from, the CMK deny rail
(aws/raw/bucket-policy-cmk-deny-rail.PHASE2-DO-NOT-APPLY.json). Do not merge
these two files into one — they have different preconditions (CloudTrail /
writer-enumeration for the encryption-header deny; a bound CMK for the CMK
rail) and different owners for clearing them.
WHAT REMAINS IN THIS FILE: TLS-only enforcement (DenyInsecureTransport).
aws:SecureTransport is a connection-layer property, not a per-request
header a writer can forget — no 'unaudited writer' failure mode, no
multipart interaction.
APPLY (founder only): aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket agrisync-raw-ap-south-1 --policy file://bucket-policy.json --region ap-south-1
(apply-config.sh does this as part of the single transaction.)
VERIFY: aws s3api get-bucket-policy --bucket agrisync-raw-ap-south-1 --region ap-south-1 | jq -r '.Policy | fromjson | .Statement[].Sid'
